stem: Crude oil is a natural source of hydrocarbons that are used as fuels.

parts.label: (a)(i)
parts.stem:
Hydrocarbons with low relative molecular mass, $M_{\text{r}}$, are used as fuels in industry, in the home and for transport.

There is a high demand for the hydrocarbons with low $M_{\text{r}}$.
parts.text: Name the process by which long-chain hydrocarbons are broken down into shorter-chain hydrocarbons.

parts.label: (a)(ii)
parts.text: Give one reason why hydrocarbons with low $M_{\text{r}}$ are suitable for use as fuels.

parts.label: (a)(iii)
parts.text:
Incomplete combustion of hydrocarbons can release carbon monoxide, $\text{CO}$, into the atmosphere.

Write an equation for the formation of $\text{CO}$ from the incomplete combustion of butene, $\text{C}_4\text{H}_8$.

parts.label: (a)(iv)
parts.text:
Identify an analytical technique that can be used to monitor the levels of $\text{CO}$ in the atmosphere.

Outline how this analytical technique may be used to monitor the levels of $\text{CO}$.

parts.label: (b)(i)
parts.stem: Thiophene, $\text{C}_4\text{H}_4\text{S(l)}$, is an organic compound that is found as a contaminant in crude oil.
parts.text:
Construct the equation for the complete combustion of thiophene, $\text{C}_4\text{H}_4\text{S(l)}$.

Include state symbols in your answer.

parts.label: (b)(ii)
parts.text:
A student carries out an experiment to determine the enthalpy change of combustion of $\text{C}_4\text{H}_4\text{S(l)}$.

Explain the meaning of the term enthalpy change of combustion.

parts.label: (b)(iii)
parts.text:
The student uses the following apparatus in the experiment.

{{figure:visual_auto_01.png}}

| mass of water in copper container / g | 200 |
| :--- | :--- |
| initial temperature of water / $^{\circ}\text{C}$ | 18.5 |
| highest temperature of water / $^{\circ}\text{C}$ | 37.5 |

Calculate the heat energy released, in J, by the reaction.

Assume that $4.18\text{ J}$ of heat energy changes the temperature of $1.0\text{ cm}^3$ of water by $1.0^{\circ}\text{C}$.

Assume no heat is lost to the surroundings.

parts.label: (b)(iv)
parts.text:
The student used $0.63\text{ g}$ of $\text{C}_4\text{H}_4\text{S(l)}$ in the experiment.

Calculate the enthalpy change of combustion of thiophene, $\Delta H_{\text{c}}(\text{C}_4\text{H}_4\text{S(l)})$. Include a sign in your answer.
